paper.title_en: Optimal Pure Quantum (r, δ)-Locally Recoverable Codes From Matrix-Product Construction
paper.abstract_en: Locally recoverable codes (LRCs) are classical error-correcting codes widely used in large-scale distributed and cloud storage systems. Quantum locally recoverable codes of locality <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta)$ </tex-math></inline-formula> (quantum <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-LRCs) are the quantum counterpart of classical <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-LRCs. They allow us to correct erasures at several positions using a trace-preserving quantum operation acting on qudits of a larger set of positions. Quantum <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-LRCs, <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathcal {Q}(\mathcal {C})$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, can be constructed from classical Euclidean (or Hermitian) dual-containing codes <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathcal {C}$ </tex-math></inline-formula>, and their recovery abilities are upper bounded by the minimum distance of the Euclidean (or Hermitian) dual of those codes. Parameters and localities of pure quantum <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-LRCs satisfy a Singleton-like bound; codes attaining equality are referred to as optimal. We consider matrix-product codes (MPCs) <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathcal {C}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> and give constituent (or defining) matrices and conditions on the constituent codes such that the codes <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\mathcal {C}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> satisfy the conditions to provide quantum <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-LRCs. As a consequence, we are able to determine their locality and parameters. Furthermore, we determine families of optimal pure quantum <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$(r,\delta)$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-LRCs derived from them.
